1.solutions: Integration by parts gives that \(\int x^{29} \ln x \, dx = \frac{x^{30}(30\ln x - 1)}{900}\) - evaluating gives us \(\boxed{-\frac{1}{900}}\).

3.solutions:
It is obvious that this sum should be some version of the exponential function. It can be resolved as derivatives of the exponential by noticing: \[(k+1)^3 = 1 + 7k + 6k(k-1) + k(k-1)(k-2)\]

Inserting this we can see that these represent 0 to 3 derivatives of the exponential function evaluated at 1. The result follows.
